Latin word

argūmentum

argūmentum, argūmentī n.

noun, second declension

an argument, a proof; the contents of a book, a letter or a play: its subject; evidence, proof; a sign from which something is inferred; the plot, the story of a play or a poem; the subject or plot of a play, a story or a letter

In this lexicon

  • argument

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Top. 8: argūmentum autem ratiōnem, quae reī dubiae faciat fidem

  • contents

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. argūmentum: “contents, subject, theme”

  • evidence

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 10.12a.3: mihi argūmentō est rēctē esse in Hispāniīs; Cic. Phil. 2.40: magnō argūmentō est

  • plot

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Ad. 22: argūmentum fābulae; Ter. And. 6: argūmentum narret; Liv. 7.2.8

  • subject

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.10.1: nūllō argūmentō prōpositō; Quint. 5.10.9 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 32; M-O s.v. subject (topic)

  • absentiae argūmentum: alibi

    modern

Examples

  • itaque licet dēfīnīre locum esse argūmentī sēdem, argūmentum autem ratiōnem, quae reī dubiae faciat fidem

    so we may define a topic as the home of an argument, and an argument as reasoning that makes a doubtful point believableCic. Top. 8

    In the entry for argument

  • Massiliēnsium factum cum ipsum per sē lūculentum est tum mihi argūmentō est rēctē esse in Hispāniīs.

    What the people of Massilia have done is splendid in itself, and it is also evidence to me that things are going well in Spain.Cic. Att. 10.12a.3

    In the entry for evidence

  • quod autem idem maestitiam meam reprehendit, idem jocum, magnō argūmentō est mē in utrōque fuisse moderātum

    and the fact that the same man finds fault both with my gloom and with my joking is strong evidence that I kept the mean in bothCic. Phil. 2.40

    In the entry for evidence

  • Dehinc nē exspectētis argūmentum fābulae

    Next, don’t wait for the plot of the playTer. Ad. 22

    In the entry for plot

  • Nōn ita dissimilī sunt argūmentō, sed tamen dissimilī ōrātiōne sunt factae ac stilō.

    Their plots are not so different, but they are written in a different language and style.Ter. And. 11–12

    In the entry for plot

  • Līvius post aliquot annīs, quī ab saturīs ausus est prīmus argūmentō fābulam serere

    Livius, some years later, who was the first to leave the saturae and dare to weave a play out of a plotLiv. 7.2.8

    In the entry for plot
